increment_status: BLOCKED on native cancellation/platform policy; no production transfer implementation or Step 24 acceptance
changes: Standalone Linux architecture counterexample using existing Runtime/Context/Operation, deterministic barriers, real pipes and /proc syscall observation.
Targeted libc POSIX AIO cancellation feasibility probe; separate io_uring setup probe inside/outside restricted runner.
Updated recovery/console/test/evidence/work-log records. Production sources, CMake, ABI, compiler, LLVM stack and dependencies unchanged.

blocker.readiness: POLLOUT followed by a permitted independent host writer filling capacity leaves even a one-byte blocking write in the syscall. Runtime stop signals the owned wake pipe, but cannot drain that operation until the host reads. This refutes readiness plus self-pipe as a sufficient general transfer strategy under the existing independent-writer contract.
blocker.POSIX_AIO: Observed on this host/libc: after an AIO worker enters a pipe read, aio_cancel(fd, &request) returns AIO_NOTCANCELED and aio_error remains EINPROGRESS. Explicit host byte delivery completes/reaps it.
blocker.io_uring: Setup only: succeeds outside restriction (fd 3, errno 0); EPERM inside (errno 1). No transfer/cancellation or platform-support guarantee inferred.
blocker.owner_decision: Settle whether native asynchronous requests may become a required adapter/platform facility where readiness is insufficient, including behavior where the kernel/sandbox denies that facility, or explicitly revise the embedding/wait contract. No option was adopted silently.

architecture_probe.method: Real probe-owned blocking pipes, semaphores, per-thread syscall observation and zero-time status checks. No sleeps; bounded synchronization watchdog. Every pending request explicitly released/reaped/joined.
architecture_probe.scope: Architecture feasibility only; not a passing Step 24 implementation test.

These results preserve the baseline and do not establish Step 24 transfers.

A later final-source default-root run failed operator_reload and temporal_ir with _year/year library diagnostics; original library bytes subsequently matched the baseline, and isolated, explicit-original-root and default-root reruns passed. External interference is a hypothesis, not a proven cause. Final acceptance uses the exact baseline library in a verified isolated root. No check was disabled; these earlier observations remain unexplained and retained for independent review.
